verdict_text:
YES

The script drops blocks {2,6,10,14}, builds the renumbering from the ordered list of surviving indices (so old→new is 0→0, 1→1, 3→2, … 15→11), copies each surviving tensor under its new name while preserving the suffix, values, shapes and dtypes, and passes the 4 non-block tensors through untouched. Renaming into a fresh dict avoids any collision. Both required checks (contiguous indices 0..11, exactly 184 tensors) run before `save_file`, so a failure exits non-zero with no output written.
